text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The government holds its regular Tuesday meeting with no major economic items on the agenda.

- Parliamentary Chairman Ivan Gasparovic confirmed that he had received a letter from a group of U.S. congressmen asking him to return the mandate to former deputy Frantisek Gaulider. Galuider was expelled from parliament after quitting the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia. Gasparovic said he had no right to reinstall Gaulider's mandate.
- State-controlled aluminium producer ZSNP expects 1996 pre-tax profits of some 400 million crowns on production of around 12 billion crowns.
- The Slovak Workers' Party (ZRS), a junior member of the governing coalition, said it would support a proposed motion to indefinitely postpone privatisation of state-controlled banks.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Parliament begins its February session on Tuesday. The preliminary agenda includes the creation of an export-import bank and a draft law on protection against import dumping.
- Merill Lynch has succesfully placed an unspecified amount of the subordinated debt issue of Slovenska Sporitelna, Slovakia's largest savings bank, on the U.S. market.
- The engineering industry accounted for 18.8 percent of the industrial production in the first 10 months of 1996, compared with a 17 percent share in the same period a year ago.
- Engineering firm Povazske Strojarne said it was seeking ways to export small agricultural machines to South Africa.

PRAVDA - Majority stakes in several companies held by the state privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), are estimated to be worth some 6.8 billion crowns. The value of the NPF's minority stakes is around 46 billion crowns.
- Police have detained a group of 31 Chinese refugees on the border with Hungary.
